questions.text: What does CPU stand for?
questions.explanation: CPU is the abbreviation for Central Processing Unit.

questions.text: Another name for the processor is the ___.
questions.explanation: The processor is also commonly called the CPU.

questions.text: The main circuit board of the system unit is called the ___.
questions.explanation: The motherboard is the main circuit board of the system unit.

questions.text: The component of the processor that directs and coordinates most of the operations in the computer is the ___.
questions.explanation: The control unit directs and coordinates operations in the computer.

questions.text: ALU stands for ___.
questions.explanation: ALU is the Arithmetic Logic Unit of the processor.

questions.text: Small, high-speed storage locations inside the processor that temporarily hold data and instructions are called ___.
questions.explanation: Registers are small high-speed storage locations inside the processor.

questions.text: RAM chips usually reside on a ___.
questions.explanation: RAM chips are typically mounted on a memory module.

questions.text: Which component interprets and carries out the basic instructions that operate a computer?
questions.explanation: The processor interprets and carries out basic instructions.

questions.text: ASCII stands for ___.
options: American Standard Code for Information Interchange
American System Code for Intelligent Interchange
American Standard Code for Internet Interchange
questions.explanation: ASCII is the American Standard Code for Information Interchange.

questions.text: A ___ is a small program that tells the operating system how to communicate with a specific device.
questions.explanation: A driver tells the operating system how to communicate with a device.

questions.text: A(n) ___ enhances the functions of the components of the system unit and provides connections to peripherals.
questions.explanation: An adapter card adds functions and provides connections to peripherals.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an input device?
questions.explanation: A printer is an output device, not an input device.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an output device?
questions.explanation: A mouse is an input device, not an output device.

questions.text: The keyboard is divided into the typing area, the numeric keypad and the ___ keys.
questions.explanation: The three main keyboard areas include the function keys.

questions.text: A keyboard designed to minimize strain on the hands and wrists is called a(n) ___ keyboard.
questions.explanation: An ergonomic keyboard reduces strain on hands and wrists.

questions.text: Which pointing device is stationary and has a ball on its top?
questions.explanation: A trackball stays stationary and its ball is rotated to move the pointer.

questions.text: A small, flat, rectangular pointing device sensitive to pressure and motion is called a ___.
questions.explanation: A touchpad is a flat, pressure- and motion-sensitive pointing device.

questions.text: Which input device is a vertical lever mounted on a base?
questions.explanation: A joystick is a vertical lever mounted on a base.

questions.text: A handheld input device that contains a light source or can detect light is called a ___.
questions.explanation: A light pen contains a light source or can detect light.

questions.text: Which device captures data directly from a source document?
questions.explanation: A scanner captures data directly from a source document.

questions.text: MICR stands for ___.
questions.explanation: MICR is Magnetic Ink Character Recognition.

questions.text: Which scanner uses laser beams to read bar codes?
questions.explanation: A bar code scanner reads bar codes using laser beams.

questions.text: A bar code consists of a set of ___ of different widths.
questions.explanation: Bar codes use vertical lines and spaces of different widths.

questions.text: Which device reads text printed with magnetized ink and is used almost exclusively by the banking industry?
questions.explanation: The banking industry uses MICR readers for check processing.

questions.text: Which device is used to input music and sound effects from an electronic piano keyboard?
questions.explanation: MIDI devices input music and sound effects.

questions.text: Voice input is entered into a computer using a ___.
questions.explanation: A microphone is used for voice input.

questions.text: Which component of a digital camera adjusts the quality of a captured image?
questions.explanation: The DSP adjusts the quality of the digital image.

questions.text: The sharpness and clarity of an image is called ___.
questions.explanation: Resolution describes the sharpness and clarity of an image.

questions.text: A single point in an electronic image is called a ___.
questions.explanation: A pixel is a single point in an electronic image.

questions.text: Which expansion card converts an analog video signal into a digital signal that the computer understands?
questions.explanation: A video capture card converts analog video into digital signals.

questions.text: A video camera whose output displays on a Web page is called a ___.
questions.explanation: A Web cam displays its output on a Web page.

questions.text: Output is data that has been ___.
questions.explanation: Output is data that has been processed into a useful form.

questions.text: Which of the following displays text and graphics on the screen?
questions.explanation: A monitor is a display device for text and graphics.

questions.text: LCD stands for ___.
questions.explanation: LCD is Liquid Crystal Display.

questions.text: Which unit is used to measure the brightness of a display?
questions.explanation: Nits are used to measure display brightness.

questions.text: CRT stands for ___.
questions.explanation: CRT is Cathode-Ray Tube.

questions.text: Which type of printer sprays tiny drops of liquid ink onto paper?
questions.explanation: Ink-jet printers spray tiny drops of liquid ink.

questions.text: Printed information is also called a ___.
questions.explanation: Printed output is called a hard copy or printout.

questions.text: Which printer produces printed images when tiny wire pins strike an inked ribbon?
questions.explanation: A dot-matrix printer uses wire pins that strike an inked ribbon.

questions.text: A single device that prints, scans, copies and sometimes faxes is called a ___.
questions.explanation: A multifunction peripheral is an all-in-one device.

questions.text: Which printer generates images by pushing electrically heated pins against heat-sensitive paper?
questions.explanation: Thermal printers use heated pins and heat-sensitive paper.

questions.text: Which device is used to produce high-quality drawings?
questions.explanation: Plotters are used to produce high-quality drawings.

questions.text: Which of the following is an audio output device?
questions.explanation: Speakers are audio output devices.

questions.text: A device that takes the images on a computer screen and projects them on a larger screen is a ___.
questions.explanation: A data projector projects computer screen images onto a larger screen.

questions.text: A touch-sensitive device resembling a dry-erase board that displays the image on a connected computer screen is a(n) ___.
questions.explanation: An interactive whiteboard is a touch-sensitive display board.

questions.text: Storage capacity is the number of ___ a storage medium can hold.
questions.explanation: Capacity is the number of bytes a storage medium can hold.

questions.text: The amount of time it takes a storage device to locate an item on a storage medium is the ___.
questions.explanation: Access time measures how long it takes to locate an item.

questions.text: A hard disk stores data on inflexible circular plates called ___.
questions.explanation: Hard disks use circular platters coated with magnetic particles.

questions.text: Formatting divides a disk into ___ so that data can be stored and located.
questions.explanation: Formatting divides a disk into tracks and sectors.

questions.text: Which type of storage is solid state media and contains no moving parts?
questions.explanation: Flash memory is solid state media with no moving parts.

questions.text: A USB flash drive plugs into a ___ port.
questions.explanation: USB flash drives plug into a USB port.

questions.text: An optical disc is written and read by a ___.
questions.explanation: Optical discs are written and read with a laser.

questions.text: Which of the following is a removable flash memory device that you insert into a slot in a computer?
questions.explanation: A memory card is a removable flash memory device.

questions.text: Cloud storage is ___.
options: An Internet service that provides storage to users
questions.explanation: Cloud storage provides storage to users over the Internet.

questions.text: Which storage medium is a magnetically coated ribbon of plastic that can store large amounts of data?
questions.explanation: Tape is a magnetically coated ribbon of plastic.

questions.text: A card that stores data on a thin microprocessor embedded in it is called a ___.
questions.explanation: A smart card stores data on an embedded microprocessor.

questions.text: The size of a hard disk is usually measured in ___.
questions.explanation: Hard disk size is usually measured in gigabytes.

questions.text: Which storage device is mounted on reels?
questions.explanation: Magnetic tapes are storage devices mounted on reels.

questions.text: Hard disks, floppy disks and optical disks are all types of ___.
questions.explanation: These disks are types of direct access storage.

questions.text: A ___ is a special-purpose computer that functions as a component in a larger product.
questions.explanation: An embedded computer functions inside a larger product.

questions.text: Which device reads information encoded on a small plastic card?
questions.explanation: A badge reader reads information encoded on plastic cards.

questions.text: RAM is a ___ memory.
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile memory, which loses its contents when power is off.

questions.text: Which memory maintains its contents even when the power is turned off?
questions.explanation: ROM is non-volatile and keeps its contents when power is off.

questions.text: Which memory is used to store data while it is being worked on?
questions.explanation: RAM stores data while it is being worked on.

questions.text: A gigabyte consists of ___.
questions.explanation: One gigabyte equals 1024 megabytes.

questions.text: RAM access time is measured in ___.
questions.explanation: RAM access time is measured in nanoseconds.

questions.text: Which of the following has a faster access speed?
questions.explanation: A magnetic disk offers faster access than tape.

questions.text: The first electronic computer was designed and built at the University of Pennsylvania based on ___ technology.
questions.explanation: The first electronic computer was built using vacuum tube technology.

questions.text: First generation computers were slow and large, and their main memory was made up of ___.
questions.explanation: First generation main memory was made of vacuum tubes.

questions.text: Second generation computers replaced vacuum tubes with ___.
questions.explanation: Transistors replaced vacuum tubes in the second generation.

questions.text: Third generation computers used ___ instead of transistorized circuitry.
questions.explanation: Integrated circuits replaced transistors in the third generation.

questions.text: Fourth generation computers were based on the ___.
questions.explanation: The microprocessor powered fourth generation computers.

questions.text: Fifth generation computers are based on ___.
questions.explanation: Fifth generation computers are based on artificial intelligence.

questions.text: Which generation of computers used punched cards for input and magnetic tapes for output?
questions.explanation: First generation computers used punched cards and magnetic tapes.

questions.text: High-level languages such as FORTRAN and COBOL were first used in the ___ generation.
questions.explanation: High-level languages such as FORTRAN and COBOL appeared in the second generation.

questions.text: A computer accepts data as input and processes it according to a prearranged sequence of instructions called a ___.
questions.explanation: The instructions a computer follows are called a program.

questions.text: Raw facts and figures that on their own have no meaning are called ___.
questions.explanation: Data are raw facts and figures that have no meaning by themselves.

questions.text: Data that has been processed within a context to give it meaning is called ___.
questions.explanation: Processed data with meaning is information.

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of a computer system?
questions.explanation: Speed is one of the common characteristics of a computer system.

questions.text: The ability of a computer to perform different types of work is known as ___.
questions.explanation: Versatility lets one computer perform many different types of work.

questions.text: Computers have no ___ of their own.
questions.explanation: Computers do not possess IQ of their own.

questions.text: The fastest and most powerful type of computer is the ___.
questions.explanation: Supercomputers are the fastest and most powerful computers.

questions.text: The chief difference between a supercomputer and a mainframe is that a supercomputer channels all its power into executing ___ as fast as possible.
questions.explanation: A supercomputer focuses its power on executing a few programs as fast as possible.

questions.text: Which computer is a large multi-user system that supports hundreds or thousands of users simultaneously?
questions.explanation: Mainframes support hundreds or thousands of users at the same time.

questions.text: IBM PC, PS/2 and Apple Macintosh are examples of ___.
questions.explanation: IBM PC, PS/2 and Apple Macintosh are examples of microcomputers.

questions.text: A microcomputer uses a ___ as its central processing unit.
questions.explanation: Microcomputers use a microprocessor as their central processing unit.

questions.text: Which type of computer works on numerical data represented by a physical quantity that varies continuously, such as temperature?
questions.explanation: Analog computers measure continuously varying physical quantities.

questions.text: Digital computers represent data in ___.
questions.explanation: Digital computers represent data in binary form using 0s and 1s.

questions.text: Which type of computer combines the features of both analog and digital computers?
questions.explanation: Hybrid computers combine both analog and digital features.

questions.text: A computer designed to perform one specific task and whose program is permanently stored is a ___.
questions.explanation: Special purpose computers perform one specific task.

questions.text: Software is a collection of related ___ chained together in function and operation.
questions.explanation: Software is a collection of related programs.

questions.text: Computer software is broadly categorized into system software and ___ software.
questions.explanation: The two main categories are system software and application software.

questions.text: Software that instructs the computer to perform the tasks necessary to get a job done is ___.
questions.explanation: Application software helps the computer get jobs done.

questions.text: Which type of software controls the performance and function of the computer system?
questions.explanation: System software controls the performance and functions of the computer.

questions.text: An operating system acts as an interface between the user and the ___.
questions.explanation: The operating system is the interface between the user and the hardware.

questions.text: The process of starting or restarting a computer is called ___.
questions.explanation: Starting or restarting a computer is called booting.

questions.text: GUI stands for ___.
questions.explanation: GUI is Graphical User Interface.

questions.text: With a graphical user interface, the user interacts with ___.
questions.explanation: A GUI allows interaction through menus and visual images.

questions.text: Which type of interface requires a user to type instructions on the keyboard?
questions.explanation: A command-line interface requires the user to type commands.

questions.text: Memory management optimizes the use of ___.
questions.explanation: Memory management optimizes the use of RAM.

questions.text: Virtual memory is a portion of a storage medium functioning as additional ___.
questions.explanation: Virtual memory serves as additional RAM.

questions.text: A program that assesses and reports information about various computer resources and devices is a ___.
questions.explanation: A performance monitor reports on computer resources and devices.

questions.text: A password is a private combination of ___ associated with the user name.
questions.explanation: A password is a private combination of characters.

questions.text: Which operating system organizes and coordinates how multiple users access and share resources on a network?
questions.explanation: A server operating system coordinates resource sharing on a network.

questions.text: Windows 7 and Mac OS X are examples of ___ operating systems.
questions.explanation: Windows 7 and Mac OS X are stand-alone operating systems.

questions.text: An embedded operating system resides on a ___ chip on a mobile device.
questions.explanation: Embedded operating systems reside on ROM chips.

questions.text: A utility program is a type of system software that allows a user to perform ___ tasks.
questions.explanation: Utility programs allow users to perform maintenance-type tasks.

questions.text: Which utility performs functions such as copying, renaming, deleting and moving files?
questions.explanation: A file manager handles file organization tasks.

questions.text: Which utility searches for and removes unnecessary files from a hard disk?
questions.explanation: Disk cleanup removes unnecessary files from a hard disk.

questions.text: A disk defragmenter ___.
options: Reorganizes files and unused space for faster access
questions.explanation: Defragmenting reorganizes files so data is accessed more quickly.

questions.text: Which utility allows users to copy files to another storage medium?
questions.explanation: A backup utility copies files to another storage medium.

questions.text: A file compression utility ___.
questions.explanation: File compression shrinks the size of files.

questions.text: Compressed files are sometimes called ___ files.
questions.explanation: Compressed files are sometimes called zipped files.

questions.text: A screen saver causes the screen to show a moving image or blank screen if ___.
options: No activity occurs for a specified time
questions.explanation: Screen savers appear after a specified period of inactivity.

questions.text: Which utility removes a program as well as its associated entries in the system files?
questions.explanation: An uninstaller removes a program and its system file entries.

questions.text: A personal firewall detects and protects a personal computer from ___.
questions.explanation: A personal firewall blocks unauthorized intrusions.

questions.text: Word processing software allows users to ___.
questions.explanation: Word processing software creates and manipulates documents.

questions.text: Spreadsheet software allows users to organize data in ___.
questions.explanation: Spreadsheets organize data in rows and columns.

questions.text: In a spreadsheet, a predefined formula that performs common calculations is called a ___.
questions.explanation: A function is a predefined formula for common calculations.

questions.text: Which application software allows users to create, access and manage a database?
questions.explanation: Database software allows users to manage a database.

questions.text: Presentation software allows users to create ___.
questions.explanation: Presentation software creates visual aids for presentations.

questions.text: A software suite is ___.
options: A collection of individual programs available together as a unit
questions.explanation: A software suite is a collection of programs sold together as a unit.

questions.text: Batch operating systems were designed to control ___ computers.
questions.explanation: Batch operating systems were designed to control mainframe computers.

questions.text: In a time-sharing system, each job is allocated a ___ to use a resource.
questions.explanation: Time-sharing allocates each job a portion of time to use a resource.

questions.text: An operating system that supports two or more processors running programs at the same time is called a ___ operating system.
questions.explanation: A multiprocessing operating system supports two or more processors.

questions.text: In distributed systems, jobs are shared between ___.
options: Computers that may be thousands of miles apart
questions.explanation: Distributed systems share jobs between computers that may be far apart.

questions.text: Which system software defines, creates and maintains a database?
questions.explanation: A DBMS defines, creates and maintains databases.

questions.text: SQL stands for ___.
questions.explanation: SQL is Structured Query Language.

questions.text: The activity of setting up software to work with the computer, printer and other hardware is called ___.
questions.explanation: Installation sets up software to work with computer hardware.

questions.text: Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint are examples of ___.
questions.explanation: Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint are application software.

questions.text: The Internet is a worldwide collection of ___.
questions.explanation: The Internet is a worldwide collection of networks.

questions.text: The Internet originated as ___ in September 1969.
questions.explanation: ARPANET was the origin of the Internet.

questions.text: An IP address is a number that uniquely identifies a ___.
options: Computer or device connected to the Internet
questions.explanation: An IP address uniquely identifies a computer or device on the Internet.

questions.text: A domain name is the ___ version of an IP address.
questions.explanation: A domain name is the text version of an IP address.

questions.text: DNS stands for ___.
questions.explanation: DNS stands for Domain Name System.

questions.text: Which server translates a domain name into its associated IP address?
questions.explanation: A DNS server translates domain names into IP addresses.

questions.text: A Web browser is a program that allows users to ___.
questions.explanation: A Web browser allows users to access Web pages.

questions.text: The first page that a Web site displays is called the ___.
questions.explanation: The home page is the first page a Web site displays.

questions.text: A Web page has a unique address called a ___.
questions.explanation: A Web page's unique address is its URL.

questions.text: A program used to find Web pages pertaining to a specific topic is a ___.
questions.explanation: A search engine locates Web pages on a specific topic.

questions.text: The process of receiving information from the Internet to your computer is called ___.
questions.explanation: Downloading is the process of receiving information.

questions.text: The process of transferring data in a continuous and even flow is called ___.
questions.explanation: Streaming transfers data in a continuous and even flow.

questions.text: E-mail is the transmission of ___ via a computer network.
questions.explanation: E-mail is the transmission of messages and files via a network.

questions.text: An e-mail program allows you to create, send, receive, forward, store, print and ___ e-mail messages.
questions.explanation: An e-mail program allows deleting e-mail messages too.

questions.text: Instant messaging (IM) is a ___ Internet communications service.
questions.explanation: Instant messaging is a real-time Internet service.

questions.text: A chat room is a location on an Internet server that permits users to ___.
questions.explanation: A chat room permits users to chat with each other.

questions.text: VoIP enables users to ___.
options: Speak to other users over the Internet
questions.explanation: VoIP lets users speak to each other over the Internet.

questions.text: VoIP is also called ___.
questions.explanation: VoIP is also known as Internet telephony.

questions.text: FTP stands for ___.
questions.explanation: FTP is File Transfer Protocol.

questions.text: A newsgroup is an online area in which users ___.
options: Have written discussions about a particular subject
questions.explanation: A newsgroup hosts written discussions about a subject.

questions.text: A LAN is a network that connects computers and devices in a ___.
questions.explanation: A LAN covers a limited geographical area.

questions.text: Which network covers a large geographical area?
questions.explanation: A WAN covers a large geographical area.

questions.text: A network that connects LANs in a metropolitan area such as a city is a ___.
questions.explanation: A MAN connects LANs in a metropolitan area.

questions.text: A wireless LAN (WLAN) is a LAN that uses ___.
questions.explanation: A WLAN uses no physical wires.

questions.text: The layout of the computers and devices in a communications network is called the network ___.
questions.explanation: Network topology is the layout of computers and devices on a network.

questions.text: Which communications device transmits data to its correct destination on a network?
questions.explanation: A router sends data to its correct destination on a network.

questions.text: The amount of data that can travel over a communications channel is called the ___.
questions.explanation: Bandwidth is the amount of data that can travel over a channel.

questions.text: Wi-Fi is based on the ___ standard.
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi is based on the 802.11 standard.

questions.text: Wi-Fi is sometimes referred to as ___.
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi is sometimes called wireless Ethernet.

questions.text: Which technology uses short-range radio waves to transmit data between two devices?
questions.explanation: Bluetooth uses short-range radio waves to transmit data.

questions.text: A cybercrime is an ___ illegal act.
questions.explanation: A cybercrime is an online or Internet-based illegal act.

questions.text: Which malicious program duplicates itself and attacks the computer system?
questions.explanation: A virus duplicates itself and attacks the computer system.

questions.text: Which software detects and removes viruses from a computer?
questions.explanation: Antivirus software detects and removes viruses.

questions.text: The technique intruders use to make their network or Internet transmission appear legitimate is ___.
questions.explanation: Spoofing makes transmissions appear legitimate.

questions.text: The process of converting readable data into unreadable characters to prevent unauthorized access is called ___.
questions.explanation: Encryption converts readable data into unreadable characters.

questions.text: An encrypted code attached to an electronic message to verify the identity of the sender is a ___.
questions.explanation: A digital signature verifies the identity of the sender.

questions.text: A small text file that a Web server stores on your computer is a ___.
questions.explanation: A cookie is a small text file stored by a Web server.

questions.text: Unsolicited e-mail messages sent to many recipients are called ___.
questions.explanation: Spam is unsolicited e-mail sent in bulk.

questions.text: Which scam sends an official-looking e-mail message that attempts to obtain your personal and financial information?
questions.explanation: Phishing uses official-looking e-mails to obtain personal information.

questions.text: A firewall protects a network's resources from ___.
questions.explanation: A firewall protects network resources from intrusion.

questions.text: The process of restricting access to certain material on the Web is called ___.
questions.explanation: Content filtering restricts access to certain Web material.

questions.text: Which device authenticates a person's identity by translating a personal characteristic into a digital code?
questions.explanation: A biometric device authenticates identity using personal characteristics.

questions.text: A duplicate of a file, program or disk that can be used if the original is lost or damaged is a ___.
questions.explanation: A backup is a duplicate used when the original is lost.

questions.text: Which of the following protects a computer from electrical power variations?
questions.explanation: Surge protectors and UPS protect against power variations.

questions.text: ___ is an applied science devoted to incorporating comfort, efficiency and safety into the design of items in the workplace.
questions.explanation: Ergonomics incorporates comfort, efficiency and safety in workplace design.

questions.text: Computer ethics are the ___ that govern the use of computers and information systems.
questions.explanation: Computer ethics are moral guidelines for computer use.

questions.text: Green computing involves ___.
options: Reducing electricity and environmental waste while using a computer
questions.explanation: Green computing reduces electricity and environmental waste.

questions.text: Which of the following is a health concern resulting from the widespread use of computers?
questions.explanation: Carpal tunnel syndrome is a known computer-related health concern.

questions.text: The right of individuals to deny or restrict the collection and use of information about them is called ___.
questions.explanation: Information privacy is the right to restrict collection and use of personal information.

questions.text: A sacrificial computer system intended to attract cyberattacks is known as a ___.
questions.explanation: A honeypot is a sacrificial system used to attract cyberattacks.

questions.text: Which shortcut key cuts selected text in MS Word?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+X is the shortcut for cutting selected text.

questions.text: Which shortcut key copies selected text in MS Word?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+C is the shortcut for copying selected text.

questions.text: Which shortcut key pastes copied or cut text in MS Word?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+V is the shortcut for pasting text.

questions.text: The shortcut key used to right-align a paragraph in MS Word is ___.
questions.explanation: Ctrl+R right-aligns a paragraph in MS Word.

questions.text: Word documents are saved with the file extension ___.
questions.explanation: Word documents are saved with the .docx extension.

questions.text: In MS Word, the Find and Replace commands are located in the ___ group of the Home tab.
questions.explanation: Find and Replace are in the Editing group of the Home tab.

questions.text: Which MS Word feature changes text from lowercase to UPPERCASE?
questions.explanation: Change Case changes text between cases such as UPPERCASE.

questions.text: In MS Excel, columns are identified by ___.
questions.explanation: Excel columns are identified by letters.

questions.text: Which Excel function adds up a range of numbers?
questions.explanation: The SUM function adds up a range of numbers.

questions.text: The Excel shortcut keys for inserting the SUM (AutoSum) function are ___.
questions.explanation: Alt + = inserts the AutoSum function in Excel.

questions.text: The NOT function in Excel ___.
options: Returns TRUE if all conditions are true
Changes TRUE to FALSE and FALSE to TRUE
questions.explanation: The NOT function reverses TRUE to FALSE and FALSE to TRUE.

questions.text: Which Excel function removes unnecessary spaces from a string of text?
questions.explanation: The TRIM function removes unnecessary spaces from text.

questions.text: To add a border to a cell in Excel, you click the Border list arrow on the ___ tab.
questions.explanation: The Border command is on the Home tab in Excel.

questions.text: Which tab in Excel contains the Sort & Filter commands?
questions.explanation: The Sort & Filter group is on the Data tab.

questions.text: To create a chart from selected data in Excel, you use the ___ tab.
questions.explanation: Charts are created using the Insert tab in Excel.

questions.text: The Excel Wrap Text command is located on the ___ tab.
questions.explanation: Wrap Text is on the Home tab in Excel.

questions.text: To fit a worksheet to print on one page, use the Fit to option in the ___ dialog box.
questions.explanation: The Fit to option is found in the Page Setup dialog box.

questions.text: Which Excel function returns the current date and time?
questions.explanation: The NOW function returns the current date and time.

questions.text: In Gmail, which button is used to attach a file to an e-mail?
questions.explanation: The Attach button, shown with a paperclip icon, attaches files in Gmail.

questions.text: PowerPoint presentations are saved with the file extension ___.
questions.explanation: PowerPoint presentations use the .pptx file extension.
